description: Reference knowledge pack. The Go analyzer defines its rules in internal/analyzer; TestRulesJSON_MatchesAnalyzer keeps the ids, categories and remediation ids here identical to the analyzer. The experimental Rust companion embeds this file.

rules.title: No NVIDIA GPU Detected
rules.description: No NVIDIA GPU was found in the system inventory.

rules.title: Hybrid GPU Configuration Detected
rules.description: Both NVIDIA and integrated graphics detected.

rules.title: NVIDIA Driver Version Not Detected
rules.description: nvidia-smi did not return a driver version.

rules.title: nvidia-smi Not Found in PATH
rules.description: The nvidia-smi utility was not found.

rules.title: Display Driver Resets Detected (Event ID 4101)
rules.description: Event ID 4101 indicates the display driver stopped responding and was recovered by Windows (confidence 92 and CRIT at 3+ events in 30 days).

rules.title: nvlddmkm Driver Errors Detected
rules.description: nvlddmkm kernel-mode driver errors detected (confidence 92 and CRIT at 5+ events in 30 days).

rules.title: Corrected Hardware Errors Logged (WHEA)
rules.description: Corrected WHEA events (ECC, PCIe retry) in the last 30 days. Escalates to WARN when an event names the NVIDIA GPU or its bus (confidence 75) or at 50+ events (confidence 70).

rules.title: Uncorrected Hardware Errors (WHEA)
rules.description: Uncorrected WHEA events (fatal machine check, PCIe or memory errors) were logged in the last 30 days; these cause bugchecks, freezes and data corruption.

rules.title: Power Plan Not Set to High Performance
rules.description: Balanced or Power Saver plans may throttle performance.

rules.title: Hardware-Accelerated GPU Scheduling (HAGS) is Enabled
rules.description: HAGS is explicitly enabled; it can cause stuttering in certain games or driver versions.

rules.title: Recent Windows Updates Installed
rules.description: Windows Updates installed in the last 60 days while driver resets were also logged; updates can occasionally introduce driver compatibility issues.

rules.title: NVIDIA App / GeForce Experience Detected
rules.description: NVIDIA overlay software detected.

rules.title: Overlay/Recording Software Detected
rules.description: Multiple overlays can compete for resources.

rules.title: No NVIDIA GPU Available for Hardware Encoding
rules.description: NVIDIA GPU not detected — hardware encoding is not available.

rules.title: Nouveau Driver is Active (Instead of NVIDIA)
rules.description: The open-source nouveau driver is loaded instead of proprietary NVIDIA.

rules.title: NVIDIA Kernel Module Not Loaded
rules.description: The nvidia kernel module is not loaded and nvidia-smi reports no driver version.

rules.title: No /dev/nvidia* Device Nodes Found
rules.description: NVIDIA module loaded but device nodes are missing.

rules.title: libcuda.so Not Found
rules.description: libcuda.so could not be located.

rules.title: DKMS Build Failure Detected
rules.description: DKMS failed to build NVIDIA modules for current kernel.

rules.title: Secure Boot Enabled — NVIDIA Module May Be Blocked
rules.description: Secure Boot is on and NVIDIA module is not loaded.

rules.title: Secure Boot Enabled — NVIDIA Module is Loading Successfully
rules.description: Secure Boot is on and module signing is configured correctly.

rules.title: CUDA Toolkit Newer Than Driver Supports
rules.description: The CUDA toolkit's major version is newer than the driver's CUDA runtime; programs built with it fail with 'CUDA driver version is insufficient'.

rules.title: CUDA Toolkit Minor Version Newer Than Driver
rules.description: The CUDA toolkit is a newer minor release than the driver's CUDA runtime within the same major; minor-version compatibility usually makes this work.

rules.title: PyTorch CUDA Build Newer Than Driver
rules.description: The PyTorch wheel's CUDA runtime is newer than the driver supports and torch.cuda.is_available() is False; suggests the nearest published wheel tag.

rules.title: PyTorch CUDA Build Newer Than Driver (working)
rules.description: The PyTorch wheel's CUDA major is ahead of the driver's but torch.cuda.is_available() is True, most likely via a forward-compatibility package.

rules.title: PyTorch Import Error
rules.description: PyTorch could not be imported.

rules.title: PyTorch Installed Without CUDA Support
rules.description: CPU-only PyTorch build detected.

rules.title: PyTorch CUDA Available but GPU Not Accessible
rules.description: PyTorch has CUDA compiled in but torch.cuda.is_available() is False for a reason other than a CUDA build newer than the driver.

rules.title: PyTorch CUDA is Working
rules.description: PyTorch GPU acceleration is functional.

rules.title: TensorFlow Import Error
rules.description: TensorFlow could not be imported.

rules.title: TensorFlow Cannot See GPU
rules.description: TensorFlow detected no GPU devices.

rules.title: TensorFlow GPU is Working
rules.description: TensorFlow GPU acceleration is functional.

rules.title: WSL2 GPU Device (/dev/dxg) Not Found
rules.description: /dev/dxg missing in WSL2 environment.

rules.title: WSL2: /dev/dxg Exists but nvidia-smi Fails
rules.description: GPU device exists but NVIDIA tools are misconfigured in WSL2.

rules.title: Low VRAM Detected
rules.description: An NVIDIA GPU has less than 4 GB VRAM (one aggregated finding for all such GPUs).

rules.title: GPU Thermal Throttling Active
rules.description: A thermal slowdown bit (sw_thermal_slowdown / hw_thermal_slowdown) is active in clocks_event_reasons.

rules.title: GPU Clock Slowdown Active
rules.description: A non-thermal slowdown reason (sw_power_cap, hw_slowdown, hw_power_brake_slowdown) is active; the fix is power limits and cabling, not cooling.

rules.title: GPU Running Hot
rules.description: GPU temperature is 85°C or higher without an active thermal slowdown (WARN); 93°C or higher is CRIT with confidence 90.

rules.title: GPU Fan Not Spinning at Elevated Temperature
rules.description: Fan speed is 0% while GPU temperature exceeds 60°C on a card that reports a fan.

rules.title: PCIe Link Speed Downshifted Under Load
rules.description: PCIe link generation is below maximum while the GPU shows evidence of load (active P-state or utilization).

rules.title: PCIe Link Width Reduced
rules.description: The PCIe link negotiated fewer lanes than the slot and card support. Lane width does not drop at idle, so this points at seating, slot or riser problems.

rules.title: PCIe Link Power-Saving at Idle (expected)
rules.description: PCIe link generation is below maximum but the GPU was idle (or showed no evidence of load); link power management is expected, re-check under load.

rules.title: Mixed Refresh Rate Multi-Monitor Setup
rules.description: Monitors with different refresh rates detected — can cause frame pacing issues.

rules.title: High Display Chain Complexity
rules.description: 3+ monitors on the same GPU may affect gaming performance.

rules.title: High Network Jitter Detected
rules.description: Network jitter exceeds 15ms — may cause lag and stutter in online applications. Only evaluated when --network was passed.

rules.title: Packet Loss Detected
rules.description: Network packet loss detected (CRIT above 5%). Only evaluated when --network was passed.

rules.title: Wi-Fi Congestion Likely
rules.description: Connected on 2.4GHz Wi-Fi (confidence 75 when the signal is below -70 dBm). Only evaluated when --network was passed.

rules.title: Slow DNS Resolution
rules.description: DNS resolution exceeds 100ms. Only evaluated when --network was passed.

rules.title: NVIDIA Xid Errors Detected
rules.description: GPU hardware errors (Xid) found in kernel logs.

rules.title: Software Rendering (llvmpipe) Active
rules.description: GPU is not being used for rendering — falling back to CPU-based llvmpipe.

rules.title: Wayland Session with NVIDIA — Known Compatibility Issues
rules.description: Wayland + NVIDIA can cause screen tearing, window glitches, and application crashes.

rules.title: GPU Stuck in Low Power State Under Load
rules.description: GPU is in P5 or lower while utilization is 60% or higher — the driver or power management is holding clocks down.

rules.title: Network Appears Healthy
rules.description: Local network and LAN appear healthy. If experiencing online issues, they may be upstream or service-side. Only evaluated when --network was passed.
